title: Aswan to Luxor: the 3-night downstream route
standfirst: The shorter way to cruise the Nile: three nights downstream from Aswan to Luxor, with the current. Same temples, a quicker pace. For other routes, see [[up]].

sections.heading: Why it takes three nights
paragraphs: Sailing with the current is faster, so the cruise needs one night less than the trip upstream.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: At Aswan, Philae, the High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk, and often a felucca sail. Downstream, Kom Ombo and Edfu. At Luxor, Karnak, Luxor Temple and the West Bank with the Valley of the Kings.

sections.heading: Good to know
paragraphs: Some cruises from Aswan sail in the morning, so you would arrive in Aswan the day before. Each cruise shows its sailing time. Check-out is in Luxor after the West Bank visit on the last day.

faqs.a: It covers the main sites at a brisk pace. If you want time to rest, choose the four-night cruise upstream.

faqs.q: Do I need to arrive the day before?
faqs.a: If the cruise sails from Aswan in the morning, yes. Each cruise page shows the sailing time.

seoDescription: The three-night Nile cruise downstream from Aswan to Luxor: the sites, the pace and when to arrive.
